edits.text: - Prefer a cut after a clause's main finite verb or copula (including its immediately attached auxiliaries and essential complements: objects, required prepositional complements, and restrictive modifiers) over a cut placed immediately before that finite verb or copula.

- Prefer a cut after a clause's main finite verb or copula (including its auxiliaries and any immediately adjacent essential complements) over a cut placed immediately before that verb; likewise, prefer a cut after a noun together with its immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier (appositive, restrictive which/that clause, prepositional complement, title or multiword name) over a cut between the head and that modifier.

Keep a clause’s main finite verb or copula (including auxiliaries) together with its subject and any immediately following essential complements; prefer a cut after that verb rather than at the marker immediately before it.

- Keep a noun head together with any immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier that identifies or restricts it (restrictive relative clause, appositive, title/multiword name, or prepositional complement).

edits._was: - Does the following material supply essential predicate, argument, or scope information that the already-heard stretch cannot bear alone? Missing these makes the earlier stretch incomplete or misleading.

- Is the material after the marker a self-contained constituent (completes a verb, supplies a prepositional complement, names an entity) so that translating separately preserves the whole meaning? If yes, cohesion is likely high; if not, expect damage.
